existence.reason: While CSE701 covers AI in software engineering with a weighted jaccard overlap of 0.185, it focuses broadly on data and AI models applied to software engineering tasks such as defect prediction and mining repositories. The new course specifically targets modern AI-native software development, agentic workflows, coding agents, and human-AI collaborative development processes.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct elective course.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 addresses traditional AI and data-driven methods in software engineering (e.g., repository mining, defect prediction), whereas this course focuses on contemporary AI-native development workflows, coding agents, and agentic software engineering frameworks.

CSE594A concentrates broadly on agentic reasoning for algorithmic, mathematical, and scientific problem-solving, whereas this course applies agents specifically to software development workflows and engineering practices.
CSE582 emphasizes traditional software product line engineering, maintenance, and re-engineering, whereas this course focuses on software production through AI-native automation and coding agents.
CSE581 covers traditional systems analysis, design, and requirements engineering theories, whereas this course focuses on specification-driven development for AI coding agents.
AI501 provides foundational machine learning theory and evaluation metrics, whereas this course deals with evaluating and testing software built via AI-assisted workflows.
CSE201 teaches foundational advanced programming and object-oriented design in Java, whereas this course assumes these fundamentals and focuses on AI-native developer collaboration.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Designed for third and fourth-year BTech Computer Science and Engineering students, the course matters because it addresses the rapid shift toward agentic software engineering and AI-assisted development practices. Students will be able to configure agent skills and tool use mechanisms, translate high-level requirements into executable specifications using the Model Context Protocol, analyze loop engineering patterns in coding agent workflows, evaluate automated testing and reliability metrics for AI-generated code bases, and assess AI-native software development workflows through live scenario walkthroughs. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions, supported by hands-on development and project-based evaluation.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules follow a logical progression from foundational agent orchestration and tool use to specification-driven development, loop engineering, automated testing, and comprehensive AI-native workflows, relying on prerequisites such as CSE201 to ensure that students possess necessary programming and software development fundamentals.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix—comprising quizzes, assignments, a mid-semester examination, a final project, and an end-semester examination—directly matches the course objectives by balancing theoretical comprehension with rigorous practical evaluation of agent-assisted software workflows and coding tasks.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701, which addresses traditional AI and data-driven methods in software engineering, or CSE594A, which focuses on agentic reasoning for algorithmic and scientific problem-solving, this course is uniquely positioned to apply coding agents specifically to software development workflows and engineering practices.
